text: The first synthetic bistable genetic switch (the 'genetic toggle switch') in E. coli, demonstrating engineered cellular memory, was published by which group?
explanation: Gardner, Cantor & Collins (2000) built the first synthetic genetic toggle switch, a bistable circuit able to switch between two stable states -- a demonstration of engineered cellular memory. It appeared in the same Nature issue as Elowitz & Leibler's repressilator paper. Ferrell & Machleder (1998) demonstrated natural (not synthetic) bistability in Xenopus oocyte cell-fate switching; Danino et al. (2010) built synchronized genetic clocks via quorum sensing; and Nielsen et al. (2016) introduced automated circuit design (CELLO), not the toggle switch.
